'''Ludwig Edward Fraenkel''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society|<small>FRS</small>]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Burton|first1=G. R.|last2=Toland|first2=J. F.|date=2020|title=Ludwig Edward Fraenkel. 28 May 1927—27 April 2019|url=https://royalsocietypublishing.org/doi/10.1098/rsbm.2020.0014|journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society|volume=69|pages=175–201 |doi=10.1098/rsbm.2020.0014 |s2cid=222142828 |doi-access=free}}</ref> (28 May 1927 – 27 April 2019)<ref>{{cite book|last=Tartar|first=Luc|title=An Introduction to Sobolev Spaces and Interpolation Spaces|year=2007|publisher=Springer|page=170|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=pQB1kiz_vbIC&q=%22ludwig+edward+fraenkel%22+german&pg=PA170|isbn=9783540714835}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web | url=https://royalsociety.org/people/ludwig-edward-fraenkel-11458 | title=Ludwig Edward Fraenkel &#124; Royal Society}}</ref> was a German-born British [[mathematician]], and professor at the [[University of Bath]].<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://people.bath.ac.uk/maslef/ | title=Edward Fraenkel | access-date=17 December 2011 | archive-date=8 August 2019 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190808010503/http://people.bath.ac.uk/maslef/ | url-status=dead }}</ref> He was the son of classicist [[Eduard Fraenkel]].

==Education==
Fraenkel earned an undergraduate degree (in 1947) and a [[Master of Science]] degree (in 1948) from the [[University of Toronto]] in the area of Aeronautical Engineering.<ref>{{Cite journal | doi=10.1098/rsbm.2016.0027| title=Frederick Gerard Friedlander. 25 December 1917 — 20 May 2001| journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society| volume=63| pages=273–307| year=2017| last1=Edmunds| first1=D. E.| last2=Fraenkel| first2=L. E.| last3=Pemberton| first3=M.| doi-access=free}}</ref> His thesis was on the design of nozzles for supersonic wind tunnels.<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://blogs.bath.ac.uk/fsstaff/2019/05/15/in-memory-of-professor-edward-fraenkel/ |title = In memory of Professor Edward Fraenkel &#124; Faculty of Science Staff}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
In 1989, he was awarded the [[Senior Whitehead Prize]].<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/prizes/list-lms-prize-winners#SWPrize |title = List of LMS prize winners &#124; London Mathematical Society}}</ref> He was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in  1993.
